body.statement: In the binary restriction \(J^{\mathrm{bin}}\in\{0,1\}\), let \(\mathcal I^{\ell}\), \(\mathcal Q^{\ell}\), \(\mathcal P_1^{\ell}\), the nuisance-dependent conditional-probability functions \(p_1^{\ell},\ldots,p_{\ell-2}^{\ell}\), and \(V^{\ell}=(B_0p_1^{\ell},B_1p_1^{\ell},\ldots,B_0p_{\ell-2}^{\ell},B_1p_{\ell-2}^{\ell})^{\mathsf T}\) be exactly the outcome-partition construction of Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen Supplement S8.2. With \(Q\) built from the corrected \(D\)-orthogonal first elimination \(N_B\), every well-defined \(\operatorname{span}(V^{\ell})\) is contained in \(\operatorname{range}(Q)\), and \(V_{\ell}^{\mathrm{ZTT}}-V_{\mathrm{eff}}=E_P[\{(Q-Q_{\ell}^{\mathrm{ZTT}})\phi\}\{(Q-Q_{\ell}^{\mathrm{ZTT}})\phi\}^{\mathsf T}]\succeq0\). The gap is strict in a contrast direction \(c\) exactly when \(c^{\mathsf T}(Q-Q_{\ell}^{\mathrm{ZTT}})\phi\neq0\). Along a nested equal-width refinement subsequence, the Supplement S8.2 density of \(\mathcal P_1^{\ell}\) in the binary conditional-null space implies \(Q_{\ell}^{\mathrm{ZTT}}\phi\to Q\phi\) in \(L^{2}(P)\) and \(V_{\ell}^{\mathrm{ZTT}}\to V_{\mathrm{eff}}\). This comparison is a binary restriction only; the exact fixed-cell theorem is asserted for \(K\geq3\).
body.justification: The theorem compares the exact projection only with the comparator's actual partition-dependent, nuisance-dependent construction and separates that binary audit from the \(K\geq3\) contribution.
body.gap: Supplement S8.2 proves density of its equal-width partition spaces and proposes the finite-\(\ell\) projection, but it does not reduce the multilevel continuous projection to fixed \(K^{2}\)-cell and \(2K^{2}\)-Gram algebra.
body.consumer: It lets a binary-analysis user quantify the residual variance of the published discretization while preventing that binary approximation from being misrepresented as an arbitrary fixed-basis module.
body.proof_tex:
By Proposition 10, in the binary restriction \(\operatorname{range}Q\) is the closed span of \(B_0h_0+B_1h_1\) with \(E(h_r\mid J^{\mathrm{bin}},X)=0\).  Every coordinate of \(V^\ell\) has this form because \(p_t^\ell\in\mathcal P_1^\ell\).  Hence \(\operatorname{span}(V^\ell)\subseteq\operatorname{range}Q\) whenever its denominators and Gram inverse are well defined.  Thus \(Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}}\) and \(Q\) are orthogonal projections onto nested subspaces, and
\[
Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}}Q=Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}},\qquad
(Q-Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}})^2=Q-Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}}. \tag{28}
\]
The orthogonal decomposition
\[
\phi-Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}}\phi=(\phi-Q\phi)+(Q-Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}})\phi
\]
has orthogonal summands.  Taking outer-product expectations proves
\[
V_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}}-V_{\mathrm{eff}}
=E[\{(Q-Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}})\phi\}\{(Q-Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}})\phi\}^{\mathsf T}]\succeq0. \tag{29}
\]
For a row vector \(c\), the quadratic form in (29) is the squared \(L^2(P)\)-norm of \(c^{\mathsf T}(Q-Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}})\phi\), proving the strictness criterion.

Along a nested equal-width subsequence for which the cited Supplement S8.2 density assertion holds, the closed union of \(\operatorname{span}(V^\ell)\) is \(\operatorname{range}Q\).  Orthogonal projections onto increasing closed subspaces converge strongly to the projection onto the closure of their union: indeed, for any \(v\) in that union the projection error is eventually no larger than \(\|Q\phi-v\|_2\), and density makes this arbitrarily small.  Hence \(Q_\ell^{\mathrm{ZTT}}\phi\to Q\phi\) in \(L^2(P)\); (29) then gives covariance convergence.  All objects in this argument are binary.  The fixed-cell theorem for \(K\ge3\) is not obtained by this limit.
